correctness.rationale: The source facet indexed by S|T has origin slack \(n^2-(u-v)^2\), where u and v are complement sizes, and intrinsic projected-normal squared length \([u(n-u)+v(n-v)]/n\). For \(|u-v|\le n-2\), an exact upper bound on the denominator yields a facet distance strictly larger than the claimed radius; the only remaining count types are \((n-1,0)\) and \((0,n-1)\), which give the formula. Permutation averaging proves global optimality of the origin, while the 2n tangent facets force every coordinate of any optimal center to be nonnegative in a zero-sum block and hence zero. The n=2 facet system is solved directly and gives the stated center segment.

value.rationale: The bipermutahedron is a canonical high-symmetry polytope arising from matroid conormal geometry, with exponentially many facets and a developed combinatorial and Ehrhart theory. The theorem determines a basic realization-sensitive Euclidean invariant in every dimension and shows a strong structural collapse: only 2n of the 3^n-3 facets control the maximal inscribed ball. It also identifies a genuine low-dimensional transition at n=2, where the optimal center ceases to be unique. This is a family-wide metric theorem rather than a routine numerical evaluation.
